harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: inventory-api is running as an enabled systemd service on TCP 8080. The separate batchworker account has a 128 MiB per-process virtual-memory limit. Oversized allocations fail without interrupting the API. Configuration and service health persisted across the required node restart, with the OS release and kernel unchanged.
actions_performed: Created dedicated inventory-api and batchworker accounts.
Deployed a Python standard-library inventory API with health and inventory endpoints.
Installed and enabled a hardened systemd service with automatic failure restart.
Opened TCP 8080 in firewalld runtime and permanent configurations.
Applied 131072 KiB soft and hard RLIMIT_AS limits to batchworker.
Demonstrated failed 200 MiB allocations while the API remained healthy.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and all required state recovered.

evidence.summary: Shows the enabled, active systemd service running as inventory-api, the 0.0.0.0:8080 listener, firewall allowance, and successful health and inventory responses before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: batchworker limited to 128 MiB of virtual memory per process without interrupting the API
evidence.summary: Shows the effective 131072 KiB limit, ENOMEM from a 200 MiB mapping, and continued API health both before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Shows CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before configuration and after restart.

Captures the healthy baseline with boot ID 96974ac3-f19e-45f7-9672-e880dd505cf8, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID 3743f091-f76f-4864-a4a0-0b4d7b467b6b, and full post-restart service, listener, data, limit, and firewall recovery.
